title: Restocking Fee Applied on Equipment Returned from a Stopped Project
content:
# Restocking Fee Applied on Equipment Returned from a Stopped Project

What the supplier charges to take equipment back from a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects depends on how long the lot has already been standing.

## Rule

Where equipment on the project stands in storage and it arrived fewer than 30 days before the stop day, the restocking fee applied is the project's own restocking fee, the rate its class carries.

Where equipment on the project stands in storage and it arrived 30 days or more before the stop day, the restocking fee applied is the project's own restocking fee together with a further **10 percentage points**, which is what the supplier charges for a late return.

Where no equipment on the project stands in storage, no restocking fee is applied.

## The boundary

The days are counted from the day the most recent stored delivery arrived to the stop day. Twenty-nine days is fewer than 30 and takes the first case; exactly 30 days is not fewer than 30 and takes the second, as does any longer standing.

| Stored equipment on the project | Days since the delivery arrived | Restocking fee applied |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 12 | the project's own restocking fee |
| yes | 29 | the project's own restocking fee |
| yes | 30 | the project's own restocking fee together with 10 percentage points |
| yes | 58 | the project's own restocking fee together with 10 percentage points |
| no | — | none |

## Worked rates (hypothetical, class restocking fee of 20 per cent)

A lot that arrived 12 days before the stop day is restocked at 20 per cent; a lot that arrived 30 days before it is restocked at 30 per cent. Where nothing stands in storage, no restocking fee enters the settlement at all.
